messages:
Sam: quick heads-up — i’m going to try changing the demotion signal granularity from per-page to slab-level for the offload path tomorrow morning. want a sanity check on the tradeoffs before i flip it.
Maya: curious — what made you pick slab-level? frag vs cpu cost?
Sam: exactly. we’re seeing lots of churn on tiny pages where the demote thrash burns CPU and spams the eviction pipeline. moving to slab-level should amortize the decision across many small allocations.
Raj: downside is coarser residency decisions could let hot subpages be demoted longer, increasing tail latency for some requests. do we have telemetry to measure that?
Sam: good call. i pulled a rapid prometheus snapshot — main signals: demote_count, demote_latency_ms, hot_access_rate_by_subpage. example query:```sum(rate(demote_count[1m])) by (pool)```shows spike correlated with small-batch inference bursts.
Liz: also watch backlog/backpressure signals. if we reduce demote frequency we might increase vram pressure and start dropping micro-batches. how will autoscaler react?
Sam: plan: two-pronged. 1) enable slab-level demotion behind feature flag + metric tagging. 2) sample per-subpage hotness for a tiny subset of slabs (10%) to detect regressions. if hot_access_rate for sampled slabs > 0.6 for 30s, re-enable fine-grain demote for that slab.
Maya: sampling is nice — keeps detection while lowering cost. how expensive is the sampling implementation?
Sam: adds a lightweight counter per sampled slab and occasional atomic updates in the hotpath. estimate +1-2% CPU on busy RPs. tested in staging, looked fine.
Raj: what about fairness across tenants? a slab with multi-tenant allocations could bias the sample. we need per-tenant tags in the sampled data.
Sam: yep — we’ll emit sampled_hotness{tenant=...} and also sampled_slab_id hashed so we don’t expose raw addresses.
Liz: can we also hook the rollout to the admission controller so we don’t enable slab-level on nodes already near mem high-water?
Sam: yep, will add rollout gate: only enable when node_memory_used_pct < 70% and vram_pressure_metric < threshold. infra-bot will annotate rollout with node list.
Raj: what are failure modes? if sampling misses a hot stripe we could see latent tail spikes. mitigation?
Sam: fallback: automatic short-window QA: if tail_p95_latency increases by >15% for model-serving route in the canary cohort, revert the flag automatically.
Maya: how will we surface the new telemetry to oncall? add new dashboard with sampled_hotness, demote_rate_slab, and a small heatmap of per-slab sample?
Sam: yes, will push a dashboard. also adding a small CLI debug to inspect slab samples on a host:```rwin@host01$ rwin slab-sample-inspect --slab 0x3f2a --last 60s```prints counters.
Liz: sounds reasonable. +1 to staging rollout with 10% nodes, and smoke-checks for tail latency + vram pressure.
Raj: +1 but please keep the revert window short and notify the oncall channel automatically.
Sam: agreed. i’ll open the feature-flag PR with tests and the dashboard PR. rolling to 10% tomorrow 09:00 UTC. tagging @Maya @Raj for review. :rocket:
infra-bot: feature-flag created: ff/demotion-slab-granularity (rollout=10%) — linked to #infra-rollouts
Sam: thanks all — will post follow-up after the canary run with metric diffs.
